# MeshCore Heltec V4 — stable v1.1.2

Guide date: 29 October 2026.

These images target the Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 V4 OLED family. Select the role
that matches the node's intended use. TFT and R8 targets are not included.

## Choose a firmware role

| Filename prefix | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `heltec_v4_solar_repeater` | LoRa repeater with the Solar power profile, receive-preserving MCU sleep and estimated 28 dBm TX policy. |
| `heltec_v4_expansionkit_repeater` | Repeater with expansion-kit sensors and accessory-bus support. |
| `heltec_v4_repeater_bridge_espnow` | Bridge between MeshCore LoRa and ESP-NOW. |
| `heltec_v4_room_server` | Shared room/BBS service. |
| `heltec_v4_terminal_chat` | Chat client operated from a serial terminal. |
| `heltec_v4_companion_radio_usb` | Companion protocol over USB serial. |
| `heltec_v4_companion_radio_ble` | Phone Companion over Bluetooth, including power saving and the estimated 28 dBm TX policy. |
| `heltec_v4_companion_radio_wifi` | Companion over Wi-Fi/TCP. |
| `heltec_v4_sensor` | Telemetry and alert endpoint. |
| `heltec_v4_kiss_modem` | USB KISS modem for external host software. |

The retained repeater is **Solar Repeater**. The BLE power-saving behavior
is part of **Companion BLE**; there is no separate low-power BLE image.

## Select the correct image and address

Verify the selected file against the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt` before use.
Keep the exact `-ota.bin` or `-merged.bin` suffix.

| Image | Use | Serial flash address |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `*-ota.bin` | Application-only update on an already compatible ESP32-S3/16 MB MeshCore layout. | `0x10000` for the release's standard `app0` installation. |
| `*-merged.bin` | Fresh installation or recovery, including bootloader, partition table and application. | `0x0` |

Never write an application-only `-ota.bin` at `0x0`, or a merged image at
`0x10000`. A compatible OTA/web updater manages its own destination; do not
enter a raw serial offset into an updater that does not ask for one. Before
a direct serial application update, verify the installed partition layout
and active application slot. A device using another layout or active OTA
slot needs its appropriate update/recovery procedure.

An application-only write to the correct compatible partition leaves the
filesystem and NVS outside that application partition. Do not select an
erase-all option as part of a routine update. A merged image is a recovery
installation and does not guarantee retention of existing data, especially
when changing layouts. Erasing the device is a separate deliberate operation,
not an implicit installation step.

After boot, verify the expected role/version, node identity and radio settings.
Nodes that communicate together need matching frequency, bandwidth, spreading
factor and coding rate. Keep the antenna connected during transmissions.

## Companion BLE

Pair using the six-digit PIN shown on the OLED unless an owner-configured
permanent PIN is in use. When the screen was persistently disabled, hold
PRG for approximately two seconds to restore it.

After five minutes without a connected BLE peer, Bluetooth fully shuts
down. LoRa reception remains available, and the MCU can sleep while idle.
To restore Bluetooth, select the Bluetooth page with PRG and use a long
press to enable it. The GATT service is rebuilt without rebooting; its UART
handles remain stable across these shutdown/resume cycles.

An active computer USB host, BLE/Wi-Fi connection, GPS, visible display,
buzzer or pending mesh work can prevent MCU sleep. The computer's presence
does not turn the BLE image into the USB Companion protocol: choose the USB
role for that interface. Diagnostic USB/synthetic wake test commands are not
part of these release images.

## Solar Repeater

Solar Repeater uses the local serial CLI at 115200 baud and MeshCore's LoRa
administrator interface. It does not provide the phone-facing BLE Companion
service. To administer it over LoRa, use another Companion node and the
Repeater's owner-managed administrator credentials.

New profiles can use a stock administrative password until the owner changes
it. Set a unique owner password locally before leaving the Repeater in
service. The serial command is `password <your-new-password>`; its reply
echoes the value, so keep the terminal output private. Existing owner
credentials are not included in this release or its public artifacts.

When switching from Companion to Solar, the shared identity and compatible
radio fields can be retained. Solar saves its active settings in
`/repeater_prefs.json`, with role-specific transactional temporary/recovery
files. On first use it can read the earlier shared profile; saving Solar
settings leaves that original Companion profile in place. This does not
convert every Companion-only option into a Repeater option.

A Companion profile normally has forwarding disabled. Check `get repeat`
after changing roles and use `set repeat on` if needed. Also verify `get radio`,
`get radio.power`, `get radio.rxprofile` and `powersaving`. If radio parameters
need changing, `set radio <frequency>,<bandwidth>,<SF>,<CR>` saves them and
requires a reboot to apply. Verify the settings again after reboot rather
than relying only on the immediate setter response.

For a configured periodic local-advert schedule, the CLI accepts a minimum
of 60 minutes; `set advert.interval 60` selects that interval. A value of
zero disables local periodic adverts. An inherited interval below the CLI's
minimum can be normalized to disabled when settings are saved, so check
`get advert.interval` explicitly. Flood-advert timing is a separate setting.

Power saving should be enabled for battery operation (`powersaving on`).
After the startup delay, the Solar path uses bounded 20 ms MCU sleep windows
while the LoRa receiver remains on. It sleeps only with RX armed, no pending
mesh work, GPS off, the display blank and no active computer USB host.
USB connection keeps the MCU available for diagnostics. PRG can restore a
persistently disabled display with a fresh approximately 20-second visibility
interval; ordinary inactivity blanking can be woken with a short PRG click.

Changing the firmware role retains a shared node identity when the existing
filesystem is retained. Recheck the advertised role and configuration on
your other nodes after the change.

## Transmit-power policy and validation limits

Companion BLE and Solar Repeater select the nominal 28 dBm FEM policy on
the tested high-power V4.3/KCT8103L board, with 21 dBm SX1262 input. Other
roles retain their existing estimated 22 dBm ceiling. These are FEM mapping
estimates; the release does not include a conducted RF power measurement.
RX profiles change receive gain independently of this TX policy.

The functional audit and its retained first 9/10 battery observation are
documented in the release notes. Later 32/32 USB and battery samples passed;
they do not establish a cause for that earlier miss or guarantee loss-free
operation. Physical bench results belong to the documented validation builds;
the newly compiled stable release images have not themselves been flashed
and physically tested. Current draw, full battery autonomy, sensitivity/range,
three-node field routing, a real solar charging cycle, physical low-battery recovery
and a 48–72-hour stability run were not qualified by those bench tests.
